analysis: While F1c cut the leader from its followers, orchestrators and etcd (not from the gateways), COMMITs on the leader waited for a synchronous standby. When a client gave up after P01 (10 s; completion info, §6.2 row 9), the pooler cancelled the backend's statement on context end (go/services/multipooler/internal/pools/regular/regular_conn.go execWithContextCancel → handleContextCancellation); PostgreSQL ends a cancelled synchronous-replication wait by completing the commit locally (S61: 'The transaction has already committed locally, but might not have been replicated'). Other sessions on the old leader then read the unacknowledged values (ok reads). After multiorch failed over to a follower that never received them, the old leader was rewound and the values disappeared: two ok reads of one key are not prefixes of each other (C3 incompatible-order). No ok write is missing from the final reads (C1 valid) and no failed write is visible (C2 valid). The run also has C4 non-linearizable on registers 1 and 4 (G6): reads at ~30.8 s returned values that were later absent and superseded, by the same mechanism (register writes whose completion was info).

origin_reasoning: The visibility of a commit whose synchronous-replication wait was cancelled is documented PostgreSQL behavior (S61); the cancel is issued by Multigres' pooler when the request context ends, and the loss follows from a Multigres failover. Not reproduced on plain PostgreSQL streaming replication (R15), so the origin hypothesis is UNDETERMINED.
